Hi Aiden —

Thanks for the RFI and the clear questions — this is very helpful. High level answers and a few attachments below; happy to jump on a call to walk the numbers.

Baseline pricing (hosted embeddings, per-vector):
- 1536-d vectors (standard): $0.0007 per vector
- 1024-d vectors: $0.00055 per vector
- 2048-d vectors: $0.0010 per vector

Notes:
- We price hosted embeddings primarily per-vector. For use cases that embed long documents or stream text where tokenization materially increases compute, we can provide a token-based alternative pricing for passage-level batching — happy to scope if that sounds relevant.
- Dimension matters because model cost scales with compute; above are our baseline published rates for the most common dimensionalities.
- Quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) are supported for most open models we surface; the hosted rate card above reflects the production-ready variants we recommend. If you choose a specialized quantized pack we may be able to pass additional savings (see tiering below).

Volume / committed tiers (example):
- 0 — 1M vectors/month: list price (as above)
- >1M — 50M vectors/month: 10% off list
- >50M vectors/month: 20% off list (higher commits may be eligible for custom pricing and billing terms)

Other items:
- Export/egress: outbound S3 transfer is billed at cost; if you plan bulk exports we can include a one-time export allowance as part of a commitment.
- High-frequency lookups: low-latency lookups against a cache are not billed per-call; serving cost is reflected in inference units. If you have sustained very high QPS we recommend Dedicated capacity and can price lookups under that contract.

Attachments: Redwood-embed-ratecard-v2.pdf (baseline rate card)

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm which dimensionality mix you expect (approx % of 1536 / 2048 / 1024).
2) If you want a 12-month commit, tell us target monthly vectors and we can return a formal SOW with committed discounts and export allowances.
3) If helpful, we can set up a 30-day evaluation (metered) with a modest credit so you can validate end-to-end latency and cost before committing.

I copied Ben (commercial) and Neha (solutions) to weigh in on the commercial terms — Ben, any quick thoughts on a standard 50M commit?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Core Platform
Redwood Inference
